audit.summary: The full Aut^0_N range may lack the necessary ribbon structure. The paper's H_2 admits a cointegral-fixing Hopf involution exchanging both roots of the distinguished grouplike. Local cup, crossing tensor and normalization formulas also need correction. The conditional Seifert/filtration argument and key ADO algebra receive positive checks.
limitations: The full cointegral-fixing automorphism group need not admit the required ribbon structure — Counterevidence: Section 2.4 explicitly requires fixing b,beta, and Section 3 opens with a G-ribbon hypothesis. Reading that standing condition as an additional restriction saves the conditional argument, but does not justify the advertised full Aut^0 range. The exterior-algebra example and ADO degree-scaling subgroup preserve their ribbon data. Reference [23] v1 already has the fixed-pair condition; v2 classifies it.

The full cointegral-fixing automorphism group need not admit the required ribbon structure — Counterevidence: Earlier source pp.8-9 explicitly assume a fixed pair and a square-root homomorphism, but p.13 replaces the group by the full graded r_H=1 subgroup. The degree-scaling ADO and exterior-algebra applications preserve their selected pair. No numerical genus inequality counterexample is claimed.

The right cup coefficient fails the snake identity — Counterevidence: The cap coefficient agrees with the actual pivot, and the proof states that the two maps should use g_alpha^{+/-1}. At p=2 the defect is masked because every zeta_2^{-4i}=1. The corrected pivotal formalism remains available.

The right cup coefficient fails the snake identity — Counterevidence: p=2 masks the error. The conceptual prescription uses g_alpha and g_alpha^{-1} correctly; the defect is the displayed coordinate formula, not a proof that the ADO invariant fails.

The formal tensor R_D omits the sign of negative crossings — Counterevidence: Page 11 correctly uses R^{-1}; later informal bead computations can and do use that rule. This is not a demonstrated failure of the invariant defined by the correct rules.

The formal tensor R_D omits the sign of negative crossings — Counterevidence: The local crossing instructions on p.11 are correct and control the intended construction. This is a local formula defect, not a failure of the corrected invariant.

Two comparison formulas in Proposition 5.4 omit the chosen variable/phase normalization — Counterevidence: At w=0 the missing writhe factor disappears. Restoring it cancels the -w alpha^2 term in the ADO normalization and leaves zeta_p^{w alpha(p-1)}=t^{w(p-1)/2}. Hence this is not evidence against the final intended equality.

Two comparison formulas in Proposition 5.4 omit the chosen variable/phase normalization — Counterevidence: Zero writhe hides the phase, and the corrected normalization proves the intended comparison; no counterexample to Proposition5.4's corrected identity is asserted.
Limitations: Assessment applies to arXiv2211.15010v1 (28Nov2022), not automatically to publisher version accepted12Oct2023/published24Feb2025.
Limitations: No numerical genus-bound counterexample was found or asserted. Conditional argument survives the admissible ribbon restriction.
Limitations: Local sign/scalar repairs are verified; full all-knot reproduction and all categorical invariance moves were not repeated.
Limitations: Related 2025 talk code/handout are not established as formal journal supplement or complete reproduction package; missing original code is not a defect.
Limitations: Initial review only: scientific_decision pending, human_reviews empty, independent acceptance pending.

Not performed: Full independent proof of the cited general Reshetikhin-Turaev/Turaev invariance and every tangle move.
Not performed: All external references in full or original Kauffman-Radford book theorem in full.
Not performed: Recomputation of every tabulated ADO coefficient or execution of ToyTDD4.nb.
Not performed: Independent acceptance or backend model verification.

Limits: No author code was run. Historical exhaustive-check scripts were not freshly executed here. No equivalence to an unreviewed journal version, no numerical genus-bound counterexample, and no invalidation of the pair-preserving applications is asserted.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.

proposition.claim:
Degree preservation and fixing the left cointegral, together with D(H) ribbon, suffice for the stated full automorphism range of the twisted invariant.

Ordinary Hopf algebra over C; H=H_2 from Section 5, dimension 16, k^8=1, E^2=0, kE=iEk, Delta(E)=E tensor k^2+1 tensor E, deg E=1, deg k=0. D(H_2) is ribbon with the paper's valid KR pair.

The displayed right caps and cups implement the pivotal evaluation/coevaluation and can be pasted to define the ADO tangle invariant.

p>=2; zeta_p=exp(pi i/p); basis v_i and its ordinary dual; generic alpha may be used.

The displayed tensor product of R_{alpha_j,beta_j}, without sign exponents, implements the preceding rule for diagrams with either crossing sign.

Already exposed by ordinary H=C[C3], trivial G, degree zero; no super sign or nonabelian labels are needed.

The displayed comparison equations consistently implement t=zeta_p^{2alpha} and the writhe normalization.

Use the section's declared t=zeta_p^{2alpha}, writhe w(D), and the correctly normalized pivotal maps.

repair.content:
Take an explicitly specified G subset Aut^0_{N^m}(H) fixing a chosen valid KR pair (b,beta), with the required square-root character, and require im rho subset G; alternatively explicitly assume the corresponding G-ribbon structure and its graded extension.

Replace the cup coefficient by zeta_p^{-alpha(1-p)+2i}=a_i^{-1}.

Use the tensor product of R_{alpha_j,beta_j}^{sign(c_j)}, retaining p.11's edge-label and crossing-map conventions.

Use ADO_p(K,zeta_p^{2alpha}) and insert zeta_p^{-w alpha^2} in the last comparison.
